{"self_assessment": "Impact: I laid the bottom line of the fish, the belly curve from the nose out to its lowest point, which is roughly half of the fish's outline and a big part of what makes it read as a fish. I built it in several steady stretches, all traced from the shared sketch, and it joined cleanly into the run so it fell with the rest. About 121 of 124 standing dominoes were connected to the start, so the picture was nearly all there for the judge.

Execution: I started on the bottom line early, at the 0:30 mark, and kept laying it in consistent batches. I reported when I reached the low point so the handoff to Hana was clean, with no gap or double work. I then inspected the crossing area twice and chose not to touch a domino that looked fine, which kept the table stable. After that I kept my hands off to avoid bumps before the push.

Collaboration: I communicated clearly about where my line ended and where the next person should pick up, and I told people when I was changing or leaving a spot so nobody duplicated work. I backed the team's agreement to keep hands off the finished fish and kept the mood light and the table informed through to the push.

Leadership: I helped keep the group coordinated and calm in the final minutes, with regular time checks and a clear message to stay hands-off, which protected the finished picture. I took clear ownership of my section and handed it off cleanly. Sofia's sketch and the tail work were important too, but my belly line was a central part of the outline.", "my_share_percent": 30}
